# 1 Maccabees Chapter 15 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, 1 Maccabees 15 | **Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## Council Notes

Chapter 15 shows Antiochus VII's initial generosity to Simon turning to hostility. The Roman letter (vv.16-21) is a parallel document to the one in ch.8 — the Roman alliance reconfirmed. Simon's reply to Athenobius (vv.33-35) is a significant rhetorical statement about Jewish rights to their land: "We have not taken foreign land... only the inheritance of our ancestors." This passage has been read as a proto-Zionist claim throughout history and deserves precise translation.

**Key term rulings:**
- "troublemakers" (v.3) — Greek: ἄνδρες λοιμοί (same as "pestilent men" ch.10); consistent with SOPHIA ruling on this phrase
- Simon's land claim (vv.33-35) — translated closely; no paraphrase permitted
- Athenobius's reaction (v.32): "the cupboard with gold and silver vessels" — the Greek σκεύη χρυσᾶ καὶ ἀργυρᾶ refers to a display sideboard; "sideboard" or "cupboard" both acceptable
- "pestilent men" (v.21) — "traitors" or "troublemakers" per established SOPHIA ruling; "treacherous men" (LOGOS) also acceptable
- The list of countries in v.23 preserved verbatim; no abridgment

---

**1** Antiochus son of King Demetrius sent letters from the islands of the sea to Simon the priest and ethnarch of the Jews and to all the nation.

**2** Their contents were as follows: "King Antiochus to Simon the great priest and ethnarch and to the Jewish nation, greetings.

**3** Since certain troublemakers have seized the kingdom of our ancestors, I intend to reclaim it and restore it to what it was before; and I have levied a great army and equipped warships,

**4** and I intend to march through the country to take vengeance on those who have ravaged our country and devastated many cities in our kingdom.

**5** Now therefore I confirm to you all the tax exemptions that the kings before me granted to you, and whatever other gifts they gave you.

**6** I also give you permission to mint your own coinage for your country.

**7** Jerusalem and the sanctuary shall be free; and all the weapons you have prepared and all the strongholds you have built and hold — let them be yours.

**8** Whatever is owed to the royal treasury, and whatever shall be owed to it hereafter — from this time and forever, let all of it be released to you.

**9** And when we have established our kingdom, we will honor you and your nation and the temple with great honor, so that your glory shall be known throughout the earth."

**10** In the one hundred and seventy-fourth year Antiochus invaded the land of his ancestors, and all the forces rallied to him, leaving very few men with Trypho.

**11** Antiochus pursued him, and Trypho came fleeing to Dor, which is by the sea.

**12** For he knew that trouble had overtaken him and his army had deserted him.

**13** Antiochus encamped against Dor with one hundred and twenty thousand warriors and eight thousand cavalry.

**14** He surrounded the city, and the ships joined the attack from the sea; he pressed the city hard from land and sea and allowed no one to enter or leave.

**15** Meanwhile Numenius and his companions returned from Rome, bearing letters to the kings and countries with the following contents:

**16** "Lucius, consul of the Romans, to King Ptolemy, greetings.

**17** Envoys of the Jews, our friends and allies, came to us to renew their ancient friendship and alliance; they were sent by Simon the high priest and the Jewish people.

**18** They brought with them a golden shield of a thousand minas.

**19** We resolved therefore to write to the kings and countries that they should not harm the Jews or make war against them, their cities, or their territory, and that they should not assist those who fight against them.

**20** We also resolved to accept the shield from them.

**21** If therefore any treacherous men have fled from their country to you, hand them over to Simon the high priest so that he may deal with them according to their law."

**22** He wrote similar letters to King Demetrius, and to Attalus, Ariarathes, and Arsaces,

**23** and to all the countries — Sampsames and the Spartans and Delos and Myndos and Sicyon and Caria and Samos and Pamphylia and Lycia and Halicarnassus and Cos and Side and Aradus and Rhodes and Phaselis and Gortyna and Cnidus and Cyprus and Cyrene.

**24** A copy of these letters was sent to Simon the high priest.

**25** King Antiochus besieged Dor a second time, continually pressing his forces against it and building siege engines; he cut off Trypho completely, so that he could neither go out nor come in.

**26** Simon sent him two thousand picked warriors to fight on his behalf, along with silver, gold, and much equipment.

**27** But Antiochus refused to accept them; he annulled all the agreements previously made with Simon and became estranged from him.

**28** He sent his friend Athenobius to deal with Simon, saying: "You are holding Joppa and Gazara and the citadel in Jerusalem, which are cities of my kingdom.

**29** You have devastated their borders and done great harm to the land, and you have seized control of many places in my kingdom.

**30** Now therefore hand over the cities you have seized and the tribute revenues from the places you have occupied outside the borders of Judea,

**31** or else pay five hundred talents of silver for the destruction you have caused, and another five hundred talents for the tribute of the cities; otherwise we will come and make war on you."

**32** Athenobius, the king's friend, came to Jerusalem and saw the splendor of Simon — the sideboard laden with vessels of gold and silver, and his large retinue — and he was astonished; and he reported to Simon the king's words.

**33** Simon answered him: "We have not taken foreign land nor seized foreign property, but only the inheritance of our ancestors, which our enemies had held unjustly for a time.

**34** We, when the opportunity came, have held fast to the inheritance of our ancestors.

**35** As for Joppa and Gazara, which you demand — they were doing great harm to our people and to our land; we will give you a hundred talents for them."

**36** Athenobius gave him no answer but returned to the king in anger; he reported to him these words and the splendor of Simon and all that he had seen, and the king was greatly enraged.

**37** Trypho meanwhile had boarded a ship and fled to Orthosia.

**38** The king appointed Cendebaeus as governor of the coastal region and assigned him infantry and cavalry forces.

**39** He commanded him to encamp opposite Judea, to build up Kidron, to fortify its gates, and to make war on the people; while the king himself went on pursuing Trypho.

**40** Cendebaeus came to Jamnia and began to provoke the people, to make raids into Judea, and to seize and kill the population.

**41** He built up Kidron and stationed cavalry and troops there, so that they could make sorties along the roads of Judea, as the king had ordered him.
